subject: Per-route variance investigation & proposed follow-ups
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Jul 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Per-route variance investigation: high-cost spikes & tail latency

Team — quick summary of something surfaced by the nightly econ job. I pulled a small snapshot (attached) showing three customer-facing routes with pronounced cost variance and a correlated tail-latency spike on July 19 between 02:00–04:30 UTC.

Key observations:
- route: /chat/generate (tenant: BlueLeaf) — median latency stable (~120ms) but 99th spikes to ~3.1s during a small number of requests; token cost per call jumped ~4x for those samples.
- route: /completion/assist — a handful of long token outputs (>4000 tokens) appear with unusually high KV cache misses.
- correlated behavior: these events align with model fallback to a higher-quantized variant in region-us-west.

Attachments: variance_snapshot.csv (small table), example_trace_20290719.json (one full trace)

Questions for product / console folks:
1) Do we want a dedicated per-route "variance" card in the console that surfaces median/95/99 latency + token-cost dispersion, with a one-click drill to sample traces?
2) If yes, what priority vs. other route tiles (e.g., current per-route spend/tokens)?
3) Would you prefer this be an "alerts"-driven tile (alerts when variance breaches thresholds) or an exploratory inspector only?

Suggested next steps: a short triage call this week, and if we want the tile, I can draft a lightweight spec with data dimensions.

--
Marcus Lin
Senior SRE, Observability
Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Sarah Meyers <sarah@blueleaf.ai>
Date: Sat, 20 Jul 2029 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Per-route variance investigation: high-cost spikes & tail latency

Thanks Marcus — good catch. Adding a few quick product thoughts inline.

On Sat, Jul 20, 2029 at 09:12 Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team — quick summary of something surfaced by the nightly econ job...

Product asks / priorities (high-level):
- We should definitely surface variance as its own signal. Customers (and CS) repeatedly ask why percentiles diverge from median spend. A single "variance card" that pairs cost dispersion with tail-latency samples will reduce support load.
- Prefer an exploratory-first approach for M1 (so we don't overload the console): tile + sampling workflow, with an opt-in alerting toggle for customers who want to be notified.
- UX: default time window 7d, sampling size 50 traces, and an easy button to "show representative traces" (head / tail / median).

Operational constraints:
- We need to be careful about storage/retention for traces; for the MVP, let's surface only trace IDs and sample payloads (no full request bodies) and rely on the existing replay store for deeper dives.

Customer coordination:
- I cc'd Sarah from BlueLeaf since they're in the sample and may be impacted. Sarah — we don't need anything from you yet; Marcus will confirm if we need an example request.

I'll prioritize a short spec and a mock (low-fi) for Monday. If Marcus/Jasmine think this is a P0 for the console sprint, flag it now.

Thanks,
Sooj

Appreciate the direction — quick follow-ups from the SRE side: 
- The attached example_trace_20290719.json includes the full timing waterfall and which backend fell back. I redacted prompt content; file is safe for sharing with BlueLeaf.
- For the MVP telemetry surface, we can compute these dims cheaply if we accept sampled KV cache hit rates and a small pre-aggregated histogram for token-cost per-call.

If product wants a toggleable alert, we should define breach rules: e.g., 99th latency > 2s AND token-cost variance (stdev/mean) > 1.2 over 24h. Happy to iterate.

Propose a 30-min sync Mon 09:30 PT to align on data columns and mock. I've penciled it on my calendar.

Attachments: example_trace_20290719.json (redacted)

Following up from today's sync: brief notes and a small UX ask.

- From the prototype: a combined chart (box+points) showing median/95/99 latency on left and token-cost dispersion on right seemed most interpretable for customer calls.
- Action item for UX: add a lightweight inline "customer impact" row that surfaces affected tenants and an example count (e.g., BlueLeaf — 6 calls in window). This helps AE/CS prep responses.
- For priority: I recommend putting the variance card in our "observability v2" milestone as P1. It sits behind routing and sampling work but ahead of expanded retention.

Small operational note: if BlueLeaf asks for more detail, we should coordinate an example export (Marcus + Kim) rather than sending raw traces to customers.

Jasmine
Product Designer — Observability
